results.result: ClpL functions as an autonomous, general disaggregase with activity comparable to or exceeding ClpG and superior to the canonical DnaK/ClpB system across multiple substrates. ClpL from L. monocytogenes showed substantial disaggregation activity toward heat-aggregated luciferase (0.67-fold reduced compared to ClpG, 3.1-fold higher than Lm KJE/ClpB), and high activity toward GFP, α-glucosidase, and MDH. L. gasseri ClpL exhibited similar high disaggregation activity, explaining why ΔclpL cells are heat-sensitive.
results.evaluation: Claims C26-C51 collectively demonstrate ClpL's autonomous disaggregase function through multiple in vitro assays with diverse substrates (luciferase, MDH, GFP, α-glucosidase), statistical comparisons to ClpG and KJE/ClpB systems, ATP-dependence controls (C33), and functional validation in L. gasseri (C48-C51). The data consistently show ClpL activity is superior to canonical systems and comparable to ClpG, with appropriate statistical analysis (p-values provided).

results.result: ClpL and ClpG exhibit enhanced threading power compared to canonical ClpB disaggregase, as demonstrated by their ability to unfold tightly folded YFP domains during disaggregation. ClpL showed rapid loss of YFP fluorescence that was even faster than ClpG, while Ec KJE/ClpB and Lm KJE/ClpB did not unfold YFP during disaggregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C54 and C150 are supported by the luciferase-YFP unfolding assay (Figure 2B), which provides direct experimental evidence for differential threading power. The assay design is appropriate (using a fusion protein with a folded domain as a reporter), and results are consistent with prior literature (C53 cites Haslberger et al., 2008; Katikaridis et al., 2019). The conclusion about enhanced threading power logically follows from the YFP unfolding data.

results.result: ClpL exhibits superior thermostability compared to DnaK, enabling function at extreme temperatures. Lm ClpL and ClpB showed comparable melting temperatures (60-63°C), while Lm DnaK had much lower thermal stability (TM: 47-50°C). Although DnaK unfolding at 55-58°C was reversible, incubation at 55°C would cause DnaK unfolding and abrogate KJE/ClpB disaggregation activity, while ClpL's higher thermal stability provides disaggregation power at 55°C.
results.evaluation: Claims C61-C65 and C153-C156 are supported by thermal stability measurements using SYPRO Orange binding and nanoDSF (Figure 2C/D), with appropriate controls and statistical analysis. The inference about functional implications at 55°C (C64-C65, C154) is reasonable given the measured TM values and known protective effects of ClpL. Comparison with E. coli ClpG/DnaK (C155) is supported by citations. The conclusion links thermostability data to functional advantage at extreme temperatures.

results.result: The N-terminal domain (NTD) of ClpL is essential for disaggregation activity and mediates aggregate targeting, enabling autonomous function. Deletion of the NTD (ΔN: ΔA2-N61) resulted in total loss of disaggregation activity toward luciferase and MDH aggregates, despite only modest reduction in ATPase activity (65% of WT). In vivo, expression of clpL but not ΔN-clpL restored luciferase reactivation and thermotolerance in E. coli ΔclpB and dnaK103 mutant cells. Fusion of ClpL NTD to ClpB (LN-ClpB*) converted ClpB into a stand-alone disaggregase.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C80 and C157 are supported by multiple complementary experiments: in vitro disaggregation assays (C71, Figure 3A), ATPase measurements (C72-C73, Figure 3B), in vivo luciferase reactivation (C74-C75, Figure 3C), thermotolerance assays (C76, Figure 3D/E), and gain-of-function experiments with LN-ClpB* chimera (C79-C80, Figure 3G). The disproportionate loss of disaggregation vs. ATPase activity (C73) argues against structural defects and supports a specific role in aggregate targeting. The LN-ClpB* experiment provides strong evidence for NTD sufficiency in conferring autonomous function.

results.result: The ClpL NTD adopts a partially folded, highly mobile structure with a stable hydrophobic core formed by α2 and β-sheet, while α1 forms only transiently. AlphaFold2 predicted two α-helices and a β-sheet, but NMR data revealed that α1 forms transiently without interacting with α2. The NTD is highly mobile with the N-terminal region (up to A34) more flexible than the α2/β-sheet core, and secondary structure elements are mobile relative to each other in the ps-ns timescale.
results.evaluation: Claims C83-C97 are supported by complementary structural biology approaches: AlphaFold2 predictions (C83-C87), NMR spectroscopy including 15N-HSQC (C88), secondary chemical shifts (C89-C90), NOE analysis (C91-C93), and 15N spin relaxation measurements (C94-C95). The NMR data appropriately validate and refine the AlphaFold2 predictions, showing that while the overall fold is partially correct, α1 is more dynamic than predicted. The conclusion about mobility and partial folding (C96-C97) is well-supported by multiple NMR parameters (R1, R2, heteronuclear NOE values).

results.result: Aromatic residues in the ClpL NTD are crucial for aggregate recognition and disaggregation activity. Sequence analysis revealed increased frequency of asparagine, glutamine, and phenylalanine residues, with aromatic and N/Q residues clustered in patches A-E outside the α2/β-sheet core. Replacement of all aromatic residues (all Aro/Ala) abrogated disaggregation, while mutating all N/Q residues had no effect. Patch A and C mutants showed reduced or lost disaggregation activities, and loss of activity in ΔN and all Aro/Ala mutants correlated with deficiency in binding aggregated luciferase.
results.evaluation: Claims C98-C113 are supported by sequence analysis (C98-C101, Figure 4C-D) and systematic mutagenesis studies (C105-C111, Figure 4E-G and supplements). The experimental design appropriately tests the role of aromatic vs. N/Q residues through comprehensive mutagenesis (individual patches, all aromatic, all N/Q, individual residues). ATPase controls (C102-C104) exclude indirect effects on protein folding/assembly. Aggregate binding assays (C109, Figure 4G) provide mechanistic support for the role of aromatic residues. Statistical analysis is provided for all comparisons. The conclusion about aromatic residue importance (C110, C113) is well-justified by converging evidence.

results.result: ClpL requires simultaneous binding of multiple NTDs (approximately 4-5) to protein aggregates for high disaggregation activity, achieving specificity through avidity effects. Mixing experiments with LN-ClpB*/ΔN-ClpB* revealed that 4-5 NTDs must be present in a hexamer for high activity. Addition of up to 50-fold excess of isolated ClpL NTD did not reduce disaggregation activities of LN-ClpB* or ClpL, suggesting vast increase in binding affinity of hexamers harboring multiple NTDs.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C120 and C161-C162 are supported by well-designed mixing experiments (Figure 5A-B) using the LN-ClpB*/ΔN-ClpB* system that exploits subunit exchange. The experimental approach includes appropriate controls (ATPase-deficient mutant poisoning, C117) and theoretical modeling to determine the number of NTDs required (C118). The competition experiment with isolated NTD (C119, Figure 5C-D) provides strong evidence for avidity effects, as isolated NTD cannot compete despite having the same binding determinants. Statistical analysis is provided (p-values for ANOVA). The inference about avidity effects (C120, C162) logically follows from the experimental data.

results.result: ClpL displays remarkable structural plasticity, forming diverse assembly states including single hexameric and heptameric rings, dimers of rings, and tetrahedral structures. EM analysis revealed that ATPγS-bound ClpL adopts these diverse states. Dimers and tetramers form by MD-MD interactions, as MD deletion or point mutants (E352A, F354A) only form single rings. L. gasseri ClpL, which is highly active, forms hexamers as the most abundant state (69%), suggesting single rings are functional disaggregases.
results.evaluation: Claims C124-C136 and C172 are supported by negative stain EM (Figure 6B-C), SEC analysis (Figure 6—supplement 1A), and functional assays of MD mutants (C131-C133, Figure 6D-E). The EM data show clear 2D class averages of different assembly states with quantification. The role of MD in higher-order assembly is demonstrated by deletion and point mutants that eliminate dimers/tetramers. The inference that single rings are functional (C135-C136) is supported by activity of MD mutants and Lg ClpL composition. However, the conclusion questions prior work (Kim et al., 2020) about heptamers being the active species, which could benefit from more direct functional comparison of hexamers vs. heptamers.

results.result: Stabilizing ClpL ring dimers through covalent disulfide bonds strongly reduces disaggregation activity. ClpL-T355C purified under reducing conditions showed modest reductions in activity, but showed much stronger activity gain under reducing conditions compared to WT (6.6-fold vs 2.8-fold). In the absence of DTT, ClpL-T355C showed massive loss in disaggregation activity but became fully active upon DTT re-addition (18.2-fold increase).
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C140 are supported by well-controlled crosslinking experiments (Figure 6F-G and supplements) with appropriate controls (oxidized WT as treatment control). The experimental design addresses the DTT sensitivity of the luciferase assay by using both luciferase refolding and YFP unfolding assays. The much stronger effect in T355C compared to WT (C138-C139) provides strong evidence that the effect is due to disulfide-mediated stabilization of dimers rather than general DTT effects. EM confirmation of dimer formation (Figure 6—supplement 2C) and SDS-PAGE verification of crosslinking (Figure 6F) support the interpretation. The conclusion (C140) logically follows from the data.

results.result: ClpL MD mutants that form only single ring assemblies create toxic effects in vivo, pointing to a protective role of ring dimers and tetramers in controlling ClpL activity. ClpL MD mutants (E352A, F354A) were produced at lower levels in E. coli ΔclpB cells, correlating with cellular toxicity at 42°C. ClpL-WT did not cause toxicity at comparable levels, but higher production levels exerted toxic effects. Toxicity was dependent on NTD presence, as ΔN-ClpL showed no toxicity.
results.evaluation: Claims C141-C146 and C183 are supported by in vivo expression and toxicity assays (Figure 6—supplement 3A-B). The correlation between reduced production levels and toxicity (C141-C142) is documented, and the NTD-dependence of toxicity (C144) is clearly demonstrated. The inference that single-ring assemblies are toxic (C145-C146) logically connects the structural data (MD mutants form only single rings) with the toxicity phenotype. However, the mechanism of toxicity is not directly demonstrated—it could be due to inappropriate substrate engagement, sequestration of cellular factors, or other effects. The conclusion about protective roles of higher-order assemblies (C146, C183) is reasonable but somewhat speculative.

results.result: ClpL and DnaK systems compete for aggregate binding rather than cooperating in disaggregation. Addition of Lm KJE to ClpL increased luciferase reactivation 1.7-fold but did not significantly enhance disaggregation activity measured by turbidity. Combining ClpL with Lm KJE or Ec KJE led to strong reduction in disaggregation activity toward GFP, α-glucosidase, and MDH. The presence of DnaK systems reduced binding of ClpL to MDH aggregates.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C45 are supported by disaggregation assays using different readouts (luciferase activity vs. turbidity, C34-C35) and aggregate binding assays (C44, Figure 1—supplement 2G). The differential effects on luciferase reactivation vs. disaggregation (C34-C35) appropriately lead to the inference that KJE supports refolding rather than disaggregation (C36-C37). The competition for aggregate binding is directly demonstrated (C44-C45). Statistical analysis is provided. The interpretation is consistent across multiple substrates, though luciferase shows different behavior (C46), which is appropriately noted.

results.result: ClpL exhibits high, concentration-independent ATPase activity (90.1±26.1 ATP/min/monomer), and requires two functional AAA domains and an intact pore-2 site for disaggregation. ATPase activities of pore loop mutants were similar to WT, while Walker B mutants showed strong reductions. Pore-1 loop mutant Y170A retained partial disaggregation activity, while blocking ATP hydrolysis in one AAA domain (E197A, E520A) or mutating pore-2 (Y504A) abrogated disaggregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C70 are supported by systematic mutagenesis of AAA domains (Figure 3—supplement 1B-D) with appropriate controls. The ATPase measurements (C66-C67) establish baseline activity and show that pore loop mutations don't affect ATP hydrolysis, ruling out indirect effects. The disaggregation assays of mutants (C68-C69) demonstrate functional requirements. The conclusion (C70) appropriately notes similarity to ClpB and ClpG phenotypes, providing context. The experimental design is sound with proper controls.

results.result: The AAA threading motors and aggregate-targeting NTD of ClpL largely function independently. LN-ClpB* (ClpB with ClpL NTD) exhibited reduced threading power compared to ClpL, as revealed by differences in YFP unfolding activities when using aggregated luciferase-YFP as substrate.
results.evaluation: Claims C81-C82 are supported by the luciferase-YFP unfolding assay comparing ClpL and LN-ClpB* (Figure 3—supplement 2D). The experimental design appropriately tests whether the NTD alone can confer full ClpL-like properties to ClpB. The observation that LN-ClpB* has ClpL-like aggregate targeting (C79-C80) but reduced threading power (C81) supports the inference of functional independence (C82). However, "largely function independently" may be an overstatement—there could be allosteric communication or indirect effects not captured by these experiments.

results.result: The enhanced threading power of ClpL/ClpG compared to ClpB is explained by their shortened middle domains (MDs), which lack the inhibitory intersubunit interactions present in ClpB's long coiled-coil MDs. This enhanced threading activity becomes particularly important upon extreme heat shock, which causes more complete protein unfolding and increases interactions between proteins in aggregates, demanding enhanced threading force for efficient disaggregation.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C60 and C151-C152 integrate experimental findings with mechanistic interpretation based on literature. The structural explanation (C55-C56) is supported by citation to Deville et al., 2017 and comparison of MD lengths. The link between enhanced threading and higher disaggregation activity (C58) is supported by experimental data in this study. The toxicity of ClpB MD mutants (C57, C151) is supported by citations. However, the speculation about importance during extreme heat shock (C59-C60, C152) is reasonable but not directly tested—it's an inference based on aggregate properties rather than experimental demonstration.

results.result: The middle domain (MD) of ClpL has an auxiliary function in controlling disaggregation and ATPase activities. MD mutant E352A showed activity similar to WT, while F354A showed partially reduced disaggregation (48% for luciferase, 26% for MDH) and ATPase activities (36% at low concentration).
results.evaluation: Claims C131-C133 and C174 are supported by functional assays of MD mutants (Figure 6D-E and supplement 1F) with statistical analysis. The differential effects of E352A vs. F354A (C131-C132) suggest specific residue contributions. The concentration-dependence of F354A ATPase defect (C133) is appropriately noted. The inference about auxiliary function (C174) is reasonable given the partial rather than complete loss of activity. However, the mechanism of this auxiliary function is not elucidated.

results.result: The NTD destabilizes ClpL ring dimers, potentially through steric hindrance on MD-MD interactions. ΔN-ClpL only forms dimers of rings, while WT ClpL forms diverse assembly states. ΔN-ClpL shows increased rigidity (higher TM) compared to ClpL-WT and ClpL-ΔM. NTD point mutants showed minor changes compared to WT but did not resemble ΔN-ClpL.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C130 and C176 are supported by EM analysis (Figure 6C and supplement 1C) and thermal stability measurements (Figure 6—supplement 1D). The observation that ΔN-ClpL exclusively forms dimers (C128) while WT forms diverse states provides strong evidence for NTD's destabilizing role. The increased rigidity of ΔN-ClpL (C129) supports this interpretation. The comparison with NTD point mutants (C130) appropriately distinguishes between effects of NTD presence vs. specific NTD residues. The inference about steric hindrance (C130, C176) is reasonable but not directly demonstrated—alternative mechanisms (e.g., allosteric effects) are possible.

results.result: The presence of ClpL on transmissible plasmids in L. monocytogenes poses a severe risk to food safety by substantially increasing pathogen survival in adverse environments like food processing plants, explaining the high prevalence of clpL in Listeria species isolated from ready-to-eat foods and dairy products.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C148 represent reasonable inferences connecting the experimental findings (ClpL provides heat resistance, is on transmissible plasmids) with public health implications. The link to food safety (C147) logically follows from ClpL's function and genetic location. The explanation for clpL prevalence (C148) is supported by citations to prevalence studies (Parra-Flores et al., 2021; Ramadan et al., 2023). However, these are interpretive claims about implications rather than direct experimental results. The causal link between ClpL presence and prevalence in food products is inferred rather than demonstrated.

results.result: ClpL and ClpG share mechanistic features as stand-alone disaggregases, including use of distinct NTDs for aggregate recognition. While ClpL and ClpG NTDs lack sequence or structural homology, both use hydrophobic or aromatic residues for aggregate recognition. The ClpL NTD represents a sticky tentacle with mobile aromatic residues that interact with hydrophobic patches on aggregates, similar to small heat shock proteins. This avidity-based binding principle provides substrate specificity while sparing non-aggregated proteins.
results.evaluation: Claims C149, C158-C160, and C163 synthesize findings from this study with prior work on ClpG. The comparison is supported by experimental data on ClpL (this study) and citations to ClpG literature (C158, C161). The characterization of ClpL NTD as a "sticky tentacle" (C159) is supported by NMR data showing mobility and accessibility of aromatic residues. The comparison to small heat shock proteins (C160) is appropriate and supported by citations. The inference about substrate specificity through avidity (C163) logically follows from the requirement for multiple NTDs. However, the claim that this "spares non-aggregated protein species" is reasonable but not directly tested.

results.result: Novel disaggregases (ClpL and ClpG) lack the IGL/F signature motif essential for ClpP cooperation, a feature shared with canonical ClpB, suggesting protein disaggregation is primarily linked to refolding rather than degradation. This underlines that loss of essential proteins upon heat-induced aggregation represents the major limiting factor for bacterial viability.
results.evaluation: Claims C164-C167 are supported by sequence analysis (established knowledge, C164) and comparison with ClpB (C165, supported by citation to Weibezahn et al., 2004). The inference about linkage to refolding (C166) is reasonable given the lack of ClpP interaction motif. The conclusion about loss of essential proteins being the limiting factor (C167) is a logical inference from the disaggregase function, though not directly tested. These are primarily interpretive claims connecting structural features to functional implications.

results.result: Novel disaggregases are typically encoded on transmissible plasmids or mobile genomic islands, enabling acquisition via horizontal gene transfer and spreading of bacterial resistance to severe heat stress. ClpL in other Gram-positive bacteria is either plasmid-encoded or flanked by inverted repeats and truncated transposase genes in the core genome. Prolonged cultivation at high temperatures can lead to mobilization of chromosomal-encoded clpL.
results.evaluation: Claims C168-C171 are supported by established knowledge (C168), citations to literature on genetic location (C169: Huang et al., 1993; Suokko et al., 2005), and mobilization studies (C170: Suokko et al., 2005). The inference about horizontal gene transfer and spreading of resistance (C171) is reasonable given the genetic context. However, these claims primarily synthesize prior knowledge rather than presenting new experimental findings. The connection to this study's results is through establishing the broader context of ClpL biology.

results.result: ClpL ring assemblies (dimers and tetramers) might represent storage states that reduce ClpL activity by shielding NTDs. The aggregate-targeting NTDs would be obstructed in these higher-order assemblies, precluding ClpL binding to aggregated proteins. The NTDs may increase ring dynamics, ensuring their accessibility.
results.evaluation: Claims C175, C177, and C182 are explicitly speculative ("might represent," "may increase"). While the inference about NTD obstruction in dimers/tetamers (C175) is reasonable based on structural considerations, it's not directly demonstrated. The speculation about storage states (C182) is supported by the toxicity data (C141-C146) showing that preventing dimer formation causes toxicity, but the "storage state" model is not directly tested. The claim about NTDs increasing ring dynamics (C177) is speculative without direct dynamics measurements. These represent reasonable hypotheses for future testing rather than supported conclusions.

results.result: Ring dimer formation is observed for other AAA+ family members with diverse functional roles. p97 double rings are suggested to represent a potentiated state, Lon dodecamers regulate substrate selectivity with mostly reduced proteolytic activity, and the role of Skd3 ring dimers in disaggregation is controversial with both higher and lower activity reported.
results.evaluation: Claims C178-C181 appropriately summarize literature on other AAA+ proteins to provide context for ClpL findings. Each claim is supported by appropriate citations (C179: Gao et al., 2022; C180: Vieux et al., 2013; C181: multiple 2022-2023 papers). The characterization of the Skd3 literature as "controversial" (C181) is appropriate given the conflicting reports cited. These claims serve to contextualize the ClpL results within the broader AAA+ protein field rather than presenting new findings.

results.result: ClpL is characterized as an autonomous, robust disaggregase with high activity toward multiple aggregated substrates. ClpL showed substantial disaggregation activity that was 3.1-fold higher than Lm KJE/ClpB and similar to or enhanced compared to E. coli KJE/ClpB, establishing it as the counterpart of ClpG in Gram-positive bacteria.
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this core finding. The editor states the authors 'demonstrate that ClpL has DnaK-independent disaggregase activity towards a variety of aggregated model substrates, which is more potent than that observed with the endogenous canonical DnaK/ClpB bi-chaperone system.' Reviewers describe the work as showing ClpL 'possesses a robust disaggregase activity' and 'has potent and DnaK-independent disaggregase activity,' with no concerns raised about these central claims.

results.result: ClpL exhibits enhanced threading power compared to the canonical DnaK/ClpB disaggregase, allowing it to unfold tightly folded protein domains. ClpL showed rapid loss of YFP fluorescence during disaggregation of luciferase-YFP aggregates, while KJE/ClpB systems did not unfold YFP, documenting ClpL's robust threading activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One reviewer states the authors 'found that ClpL is more thermostable than the endogenous L. monocytogenes DnaK and has the capacity to unfold tightly folded protein domains.' The editor notes the work is 'supported by compelling evidence,' and no reviewer questions the threading power data or conclusions.

results.result: ClpL shows increased thermostability compared to Lm DnaK, with ClpL and ClpB exhibiting melting temperatures of 60-63°C while DnaK's TM was 47-50°C. This higher thermal stability enables ClpL to provide disaggregation power at 55°C when DnaK is unfolded, explaining ClpL's protective effect on bacterial survival at extreme temperatures.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding. One reviewer notes 'LmClpL appears to have greater thermostability as compared to LmDnaK, suggesting that ClpL-expressing cells may be able to withstand more severe heat stress conditions.' Another states the authors 'found that ClpL is more thermostable than the endogenous L. monocytogenes DnaK.' No concerns are raised about the thermostability data or interpretations.

results.result: ClpL achieves aggregate specificity via a unique N-terminal domain (NTD) that is essential for disaggregase function. Deletion of the NTD resulted in total loss of disaggregation activity in vitro and failed to restore thermotolerance in E. coli cells. Fusion of ClpL NTD to ClpB converted ClpB into a stand-alone disaggregase, demonstrating the NTD enables direct aggregate binding independent of partner proteins.
results.evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm this finding as a major contribution. One reviewer states 'the authors further characterized the mechanisms by which ClpL interacts with protein aggregates, identifying that the N-terminal domain of ClpL is essential for disaggregase function.' Another notes 'Remarkably, grafting the NTD of ClpL to ClpB converted ClpB into an autonomous disaggregase, highlighting the importance of such a domain.' The work is described as showing 'the importance of the atypical ClpL N-terminal domain in the disaggregation process.'

results.result: The ClpL NTD structure was characterized by NMR and AlphaFold2 prediction, revealing a highly mobile domain with a partially stable core formed by α-helix 2 and a β-sheet. The α-helix 1 forms only transiently and does not interact with α-helix 2, making aromatic residues available for substrate binding. NMR data showed the N-terminal region is more flexible than the hydrophobic core, with secondary structure elements mobile relative to each other.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm this structural characterization without raising concerns. One reviewer notes the work 'identifying key residues and positions necessary for aggregates recognition and disaggregation' and describes the data as 'conclusive and well controlled.' The structural work is treated as supporting the functional findings about NTD-mediated aggregate recognition.

results.result: Aromatic residues in the ClpL NTD are crucial for aggregate recognition and disaggregation activity. Sequence analysis revealed increased frequency of aromatic residues organized in patches outside the stable core. Replacement of all aromatic residues abrogated disaggregation, while mutating N/Q residues had no effect. Patch A and C mutants showed reduced or lost activity, and loss of activity correlated with deficiency in binding aggregated substrates.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding. One states the work 'identifying key residues and positions necessary for aggregates recognition and disaggregation' with 'conclusive and well controlled' experiments. Another notes the authors 'show that ClpL interacts with aggregated proteins through the aromatic residues present in its N-terminal domain.' The mutagenesis data and binding studies are not questioned.

results.result: Multiple ClpL NTDs must bind simultaneously to protein aggregates for high disaggregation activity. Mixing experiments revealed approximately four to five ClpL NTDs must be present in a hexamer to confer high disaggregation activity, indicating ClpL increases binding affinity through avidity effects.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about this finding. The mixing experiments and conclusions about multiple NTD requirement are treated as part of the comprehensive mechanistic characterization. One reviewer notes the work 'push further our knowledge of such important disaggregases' without questioning the avidity mechanism.

results.result: ClpL displays remarkable structural plasticity, forming hexameric and heptameric rings that can interact via middle domains to form dimers and tetramers. EM analysis revealed diverse assembly states including single rings, dimers of rings, and tetrahedral structures. MD mutants that only form single rings retained activity, and Lg ClpL (69% hexamers) showed high activity, indicating single rings represent functional disaggregases.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One states 'using sets of SEC and negative staining EM experiments combined with conditional covalent linkages and disaggregation assays the authors found that ClpL shows significant structural plasticity, forming dynamic hexameric and heptameric active single rings that can further form higher assembly states via their middle domains.' Another notes the work shows 'the structural malleability of such AAA+ proteins.' The conclusion that single rings are active is not questioned.

results.result: ClpL ring dimers and tetramers have protective roles by restricting ClpL activity. ΔN-ClpL exclusively forms dimers, suggesting NTDs destabilize this state through steric hindrance. Stabilizing ring dimers through covalent crosslinking (T355C) strongly reduced disaggregation activity. MD mutants that only form single rings showed cellular toxicity, pointing to a physiological role of higher-order assemblies in controlling ClpL activity.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support this finding added during revision. One reviewer notes 'In the revised version additional data is presented suggesting that dimer or tetramer of ClpL rings play a protective role in cell by restricting ClpL activity' and states the experiments are 'conclusive and well controlled.' The toxicity data and crosslinking experiments supporting this conclusion are not questioned.

results.result: ClpL disaggregation activity is ATP-dependent and requires two functional AAA domains and an intact pore-2 site. ClpL exhibits high ATPase activity (90.1±26.1 ATP/min/monomer). Pore loop mutants retained similar ATPase to WT, while Walker B mutants showed strongly reduced activity. The pore-1 mutant Y170A retained partial disaggregation activity, but blocking ATP hydrolysis in one AAA domain or mutating pore-2 abrogated disaggregation.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these mechanistic findings. One reviewer notes 'The data presented show that the two AAA domains, the pore-2 site and the N-terminal domain (NTD) of ClpL are critical for its disaggregase activity' and describes the work as 'well executed' with 'conclusive and well controlled' experiments. The ATPase and mutagenesis data are treated as standard characterization.

results.result: Addition of Lm KJE to ClpL increased luciferase reactivation 1.7-fold but did not significantly enhance disaggregation activity measured by turbidity, arguing against direct cooperation in disaggregation. For other substrates, combining ClpL with KJE led to strong reduction in disaggregation activity due to competition for aggregate binding, as the presence of DnaK systems reduced ClpL binding to aggregates.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about these findings. The competition mechanism and lack of synergy with DnaK systems are treated as supporting the conclusion that ClpL is an autonomous disaggregase. One reviewer notes the work shows ClpL 'does not further require the endogenous DnaK chaperone in vitro' without questioning the competition data.

results.result: ClpL provides thermotolerance in vivo in E. coli cells lacking functional disaggregases. Expression of clpL restored thermotolerance in E. coli ΔclpB and dnaK103 mutant cells, with ClpL activity lower than ClpG but higher than E. coli ClpB. Expression of ΔN-clpL did not restore thermotolerance, confirming the NTD requirement in vivo.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm this finding. One states 'LmClpL can provide thermotolerance to E. coli that have been genetically depleted of either ClpB or in cells expressing a mutant DnaK103.' Another notes the work is 'in some cases, supported by in vivo data performed in chaperone-deficient E. coli strains.' The in vivo validation is treated as strengthening the conclusions.

results.result: Lactobacillus gasseri ClpL exhibited high disaggregation activity similar to Lm ClpL. L. gasseri does not encode ClpB and ΔclpL cells exhibit loss of heat resistance, explaining why Lg ΔclpL cells are heat-sensitive as they lost their central disaggregase.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question this finding. One notes the work provides 'examples of how ClpL can provide in vivo thermotolerance to both E. coli and L. gasseri' and states this 'expanded the significance of this work.' The L. gasseri data is treated as confirming ClpL's role as a central disaggregase in bacteria lacking ClpB.

results.result: LN-ClpB* (ClpB with ClpL NTD) exerted reduced threading power compared to ClpL despite having the ClpL NTD, as revealed by differences in YFP unfolding activities. This suggests the AAA threading motors and aggregate-targeting NTD largely function independently.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not raise concerns about this finding. The LN-ClpB* chimera experiments are treated as supporting the conclusion that the NTD provides aggregate targeting while threading power is determined by the AAA motor domains. The independence of these functions is not questioned.

results.result: ClpL middle domain (MD) mutants showed varied effects on activity. E352A exhibited similar disaggregation to WT, while F354A showed partially reduced activity and reduced ATPase activity at low concentrations. These findings suggest an auxiliary function of the MD in controlling disaggregation and ATPase activities.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not question these findings about MD function. The data on MD mutants is treated as part of the comprehensive characterization of ClpL structure-function relationships. One reviewer notes the work is 'well executed' without raising concerns about the MD mutant analysis.

results.result: The presence of ClpL on transmissible plasmids in Lm poses a severe risk to food safety by substantially increasing pathogen survival in food processing plants. This explains the high prevalence of clpL in Listeria species isolated from ready-to-eat foods and dairy products.
results.evaluation: Reviewers affirm the significance of this finding for food safety. The editor states the work details 'ClpL from L. monocytogenes as an effective and autonomous AAA+ disaggregase that provides enhanced heat resistance to this food-borne pathogen.' One reviewer notes the work 'provides novel insight into potential mechanisms responsible for thermotolerance in food-borne pathogens.' The food safety implications are treated as an important outcome.

results.result: ClpL and ClpG share five features as stand-alone disaggregases, including higher threading power, increased thermostability, distinct NTDs for direct aggregate binding, lack of ClpP interaction motif, and encoding on transmissible genetic elements. Novel disaggregases can be acquired by horizontal gene transfer, leading to spreading of bacterial heat stress resistance.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly support the comparison with ClpG and the broader conclusions. One reviewer notes 'The study's strength lies in the direct comparison of ClpL biochemical properties with autonomous ClpG disaggregase present in selected Gram-negative bacteria and well-studied E. coli system consisting of ClpB disaggregase and DnaK and its cochaperones. This puts the results in a broader context.' Another states the work 'demonstrating that these two enzymes share homologous activity and qualities.'

comparisons.comparison: Both strongly support ClpL's autonomous disaggregase function with multiple substrates. OpenEval provides detailed claim-by-claim analysis (C26-C51) including statistical validation, while peer reviewers affirm this as a core finding with explicit statements about DnaK-independent activity being 'more potent than canonical systems.' High agreement on central conclusion.

Both support enhanced threading power findings (C52-C54, C150). OpenEval emphasizes the luciferase-YFP assay design and literature consistency, while peer reviewers affirm ClpL 'has the capacity to unfold tightly folded protein domains' with 'compelling evidence.' Complete agreement.

Both support thermostability findings (C61-C65, C153-C156). OpenEval details thermal stability measurements and functional implications at 55°C, while peer reviewers note 'greater thermostability as compared to LmDnaK' enabling cells to 'withstand more severe heat stress conditions.' Strong agreement on data and interpretation.

Both strongly support NTD essentiality for disaggregase function (C71-C80, C157). OpenEval emphasizes multiple complementary experiments including LN-ClpB* chimera, while peer reviewers describe this as a 'major contribution' with 'Remarkably, grafting the NTD of ClpL to ClpB converted ClpB into an autonomous disaggregase.' Complete agreement on significance.

Both support NTD structural characterization (C83-C97). OpenEval details AlphaFold2 predictions validated by NMR showing partial folding and mobility, while peer reviewers affirm structural work as 'conclusive and well controlled' supporting aggregate recognition findings. Agreement on structural data quality.

Both support aromatic residue importance for aggregate binding (C98-C113). OpenEval emphasizes systematic mutagenesis with ATPase controls, while peer reviewers note 'conclusive and well controlled' experiments 'identifying key residues and positions necessary for aggregates recognition.' Strong agreement.

Both support avidity mechanism requiring multiple NTDs (C118-C120, C161-C162). OpenEval details mixing experiments and competition assays, while peer reviewers treat this as part of comprehensive mechanistic characterization without raising concerns. Agreement on avidity model.

Both support structural plasticity and single-ring activity (C124-C136, C172). OpenEval provides detailed EM and SEC analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'ClpL shows significant structural plasticity, forming dynamic hexameric and heptameric active single rings.' Strong agreement, though OpenEval notes tension with prior literature on heptamer requirement.

OpenEval details differential effects on reactivation vs. disaggregation and aggregate binding competition, while peer reviewers affirm ClpL 'does not further require the endogenous DnaK chaperone in vitro.' Complete agreement.

OpenEval notes LN-ClpB* has aggregate targeting but reduced threading, while peer reviewers treat chimera experiments as supporting NTD provides targeting while AAA domains determine threading power. Agreement, though OpenEval questions whether 'largely function independently' may overstate the case.

OpenEval includes this in comprehensive NTD characterization, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'LmClpL can provide thermotolerance to E. coli' in chaperone-deficient strains, treating in vivo data as strengthening conclusions. Agreement.

Both support L. gasseri validation (C48-C51). OpenEval includes this in comprehensive disaggregase activity evidence, while peer reviewers note this 'expanded the significance of this work' confirming ClpL as central disaggregase in bacteria lacking ClpB. Agreement on significance.

OpenEval details differential effects of E352A vs. F354A mutations, while peer reviewers treat MD mutant analysis as part of 'well executed' structure-function characterization. Agreement on data, mechanism not fully elucidated in either evaluation.

OpenEval details EM showing ΔN-ClpL exclusively forms dimers and increased rigidity, while peer reviewers affirm findings about protective role of dimers/tetramers. Agreement on NTD effects, OpenEval notes steric hindrance mechanism is inferred rather than demonstrated.

OpenEval notes these are interpretive claims about implications rather than direct experimental results, while peer reviewers affirm significance for 'thermotolerance in food-borne pathogens' with editor highlighting 'enhanced heat resistance to this food-borne pathogen.' Agreement on significance, OpenEval more explicit about inferential nature.

Strong agreement on comparative context.

OpenEval notes these are interpretive claims connecting structural features to functional implications, while peer reviewers affirm broader context comparing ClpL with 'well-studied E. coli system consisting of ClpB disaggregase and DnaK.' Agreement on comparative framework.

OpenEval notes these primarily synthesize prior knowledge rather than new findings, while peer reviewers affirm comparison with ClpG and broader context. Agreement that genetic location on plasmids has implications for spread.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation linking enhanced threading to disaggregation activity and speculation about extreme heat shock importance (C55-C60, C151-C152). Notes speculation about heat shock is reasonable but not directly tested. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewers generally affirm mechanistic findings.

Peer reviewers affirm protective role findings but do not separately evaluate these specific speculative mechanisms.
